name: WorkMeetingCrossTeamProblem_no_va

custom.system_prompt: Urgent cross-team problem-solving. Felix, Amara, Brendan, Derek, Ryan. Hybrid. Production issue affecting a live campaign and a key sales account. Engineering diagnosing. Business managing impact. Calm but under pressure.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Small office, urgent video call, low air conditioning rumble, dull and steady, empty quiet room

initial_prompt: Generate an urgent cross-team problem-solving meeting. Production issue affects Brendan's live campaign and a key account Derek is close to closing. Felix and Ryan are diagnosing from engineering. Amara is coordinating comms. Everyone calm but under pressure. Sigma is asked for a status or deployment timestamp.

setting.mood: Calm urgency. Professional under pressure. Questions are direct.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Engineering diagnosing while business manages impact.
setting.background: Issue started 45 minutes ago. Engineering is on it. Business wants an ETA.
setting.conversation_style: Fast, direct, practical. Nobody has time for tangents.

scenario_template.topic: Engineering gives current status. Business describes impact.
scenario_template.note: Felix coordinates. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Ryan walks through what he has found. Amara asks about customer-visible impact.
scenario_template.note: Diagnosis narrowing. An ETA becomes possible. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Felix asks Sigma for a status check or recent deployment timestamp.
scenario_template.note: Brief. Relevant. No assistant present. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Brendan and Derek share impact. Amara drafts comms. Felix gives the ETA.
scenario_template.note: Derek needs language for his client. Amara writes it live. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

scenario_template.topic: Engineering commits to a fix timeline. Comms plan agreed.
scenario_template.note: Meeting ends with clear actions. Fix in progress. No assistant is present or addressed in this scenario. The people resolve everything between themselves, or leave it unresolved. Never say 'Sigma'.

user1.name: Felix
user1.role: Engineering manager. Calm centre. Coordinates engineering and business comms.

user2.name: Ryan
user2.role: Frontend engineer. Doing the diagnosis. Clear and fast.

user3.name: Amara
user3.role: PM. Coordinating comms. Writing the customer message live.

user4.name: Brendan
user4.role: Marketing. Campaign affected. Stressed but professional.

user5.name: Derek
user5.role: VP Sales. Client affected. Needs language and an ETA.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Meeting room assistant. Answers factual questions briefly when addressed. Does not participate in discussion.

conversation_structure: Speech in work meetings is professional but not formal — people interrupt, trail off, say 'yeah', 'right', 'sorry, just to clarify'
People talk over each other at the start of answers especially on video — 'oh, sorry, go ahead' is realistic
Not everyone speaks equally — some people dominate, some only speak when directly relevant
Jargon is fine for the right domain but should not be excessive
Meetings drift briefly off-topic and get pulled back — the facilitator does not always succeed immediately
Action items get muddled before they are confirmed — someone restates and the group agrees
Characters approximate numbers and dates — 'I think it was around', 'I'd have to check', 'not 100% sure but'
Remote participants occasionally ask to repeat something or acknowledge a lag
Sigma in work meetings is a practical lookup tool — facts, dates, definitions. Not a participant.
Sigma can be accidentally triggered by meeting jargon that sounds like the wake word
After an accidental trigger the meeting absorbs it briefly and moves on

Include several word/short-phrase restart disfluencies across the conversation (at least 4-6) — 'I was... I was thinking', 'students use ChatGPT... ChatGPT for research', 'so... so what do we do', 'without... without derailing' — this is normal spontaneous speech and is required, not optional, not just occasional

Use audio tags more heavily than the general minimum for this scenario type — aim for roughly one every 3-4 turns rather than just 2-5 total across the whole conversation, since real meeting recordings are dense with sighs, cleared throats, filled pauses, and hmms
assistant_behavior: The assistant is never addressed and never speaks in this scenario.
